messages:
evan: heads up — we're getting a cluster of 503s for hosted inference starting ~20:04 UTC. multiple customers (ACME, HexLabs) reporting timeouts and immediate 503s. logs from one node show GPU OOM followed by container restart. tagging as incident and loop in oncall. :warning:

morgan: seen it. looks like the regression landed with the batching change rolled out at 19:55 -> increased default batch_size for short requests. reproducing locally with a long context + high batch size triggers mem spike. :eyes:

amanda (support): ACME ticket TICKET-7842 — they hit this during a nightly job that sends long prompts (~12k tokens). They saw 503s starting exactly at 20:05 and it impacted ~40% of their requests. They want ETA and mitigation.

nikki (sre-oncall): I'm on it. can you paste the container logs + which node IDs? I'll cordon and remove from rotation if crash loop.

morgan: paste of relevant log snippet from node gpu-12 (container id 0a3f2e):

```
[2026-03-15T19:59:58Z] runtime: attempting batch size 8, seq_len 12000
[2026-03-15T19:59:59Z] Alloc failure: request 48GB, available 44GB
[2026-03-15T20:00:00Z] cuda_malloc: out of memory
[2026-03-15T20:00:01Z] worker(12345): libc++abi: terminating with uncaught exception of type std::bad_alloc
[2026-03-15T20:00:02Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 12345 (worker) score 999
[2026-03-15T20:00:03Z] container runtime: container exited with code 137
[2026-03-15T20:00:03Z] watchdog: restarting container
```

chao: also saw segfault traces on another host (gpu-05) — looks like a race when KV cache resize + continuous batching happens under heavy sequence lengths. short stacktrace (from dmesg):

```
[ 1234.567890] worker[23456]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f8a4bcd1234 sp 00007ffc1a2b3c d8
[ 1234.567895] Code: Bad RIP
[ 1234.567900] Kernel panic? No, OOM killer invoked
```

evan: summary for customer-facing: root cause appears to be the new batching default combined with long-context workloads hitting >GPU memory, causing OOM and in some cases segfaults during KV cache operations. causing 503s and container restarts.

nikki (sre-oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon gpu-12 and gpu-05 from LB 2) reduce global default batch_size from 8 -> 4 via feature-flag (rollout-backstop) 3) create temp autoscale to add extra capacity 4) push a hotfix to disable KV-resize optimization for long-context on the runtime side. executing steps now. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout triggered: feature-flag/batching-default -> set 4 (target rollout 100%) by morgan at 20:07 UTC

morgan: starting hotfix branch now. quick patch will skip continuous-batching for requests with seq_len > 8192 and force single-request execution. patch build / smoke tests in CI.

ops-bot: alerting: scaled up hosted-pool-gpu by +4 nodes at 20:09 UTC (policy: emergency-scale).

amanda (support): relayed to ACME: we are investigating and applying mitigations; recommending they reduce their client-side batch_size to 1 for now. they've asked for an estimate; can we confirm when we expect full resolution?

chao: repro steps I used locally (share with SRE):
```
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-large-2","input":"<12k token prompt>","max_tokens":1024,"batch_size":8}'
```
This reproduces OOM in ~10s on our perf-1 GPUs when seq_len > 8k. also reproduced with the streaming path.

nikki (sre-oncall): updates: cordoned gpu-12, removed from rotation. Reduced batch flag pushed and fully rolled out at 20:10. Hotfix branch built and deployed to canary hosts (gpu-canary-1/2) at 20:12. Monitoring logs and 503 rate.

morgan: hotfix confirmed on canary — long-context requests now fallback to non-batched path, memory stable on canary. planning full rollout in 15m pending no regressions.

evan: any billing/quotas impact? ACME asked if they were charged for failed requests. we should coordinate support reply.

amanda (support): we will refund 503s where they retried within 5m and didn't complete (TICKET-7842). patching support reply now.

lena: for post-incident follow-up: open action items: 1) revert batching default change until we have a regression test for long-context + batching 2) add mem-pressure alerts per-GPU 3) add client-side guidance for batch_size/seq_len combinations 4) deeper root cause analysis of KV cache resize race. assigning to chao/morgan.

morgan: agreed. I'll open a PR to add an e2e test in perf-suite that runs long-context across batching matrix (batch_size [1,4,8], seq_len [2k,8k,12k]) and assert no OOM/segfault.

nikki (sre-oncall): current status at 20:21 UTC: 503 rate dropped to baseline after rollout and scale-up. still watching logs for segfaults; none on canaries. escalation reduced. will keep thread updated.

evan: thanks all — please post the postmortem link when ready and include customer impact summary + timeline for ACME. closing in 1h if stable. :white_check_mark:
